sanskrit: asyāraṇyasya mahatī devatā vā mahībhṛtaḥ asyā nu nadyāḥ kalyāṇi vada satyam anindite
english: Are you the great deity of this forest, or of this mountain, or of this river? O auspicious one, O blameless one, tell us the truth.

sanskrit: sābravīt tān ṛṣīn nāham araṇyasyāsya devatā na cāpy asya girer viprā na nadyā devatāpy aham
english: She said to those sages: I am not the deity of this forest, O brahmins, nor of this mountain, nor of this river — I am no deity at all.

sanskrit: mānuṣīṃ māṃ vijānīta yūyaṃ sarve tapodhanāḥ vistareṇābhidhāsyāmi tan me śṛṇuta sarvaśaḥ
english: Know me as a mortal woman, all of you who are rich in austerity. I shall tell you at length — listen to me fully.

sanskrit: vidarbheṣu mahīpālo bhīmo nāma mahādyutiḥ tasya māṃ tanayāṃ sarve jānīta dvijasattamāḥ
english: In Vidarbha there is a great king named Bhima, blazing in glory. Know me as his daughter, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: niṣadhādhipatir dhīmān nalo nāma mahāyaśāḥ vīraḥ saṃgrāmajid vidvān mama bhartā viśāṃ patiḥ
english: The wise lord of Nishadha, famed Nala of great renown, a hero victorious in battle, a learned man — he is my husband, the lord of his people.

sanskrit: devatābhyarcanaparo dvijātijanavatsalaḥ goptā niṣadhavaṃśasya mahābhāgo mahādyutiḥ
english: Devoted to the worship of the gods, affectionate toward the twice-born, the protector of the Nishadha lineage — he is greatly fortunate and blazing in splendor.

sanskrit: satyavāg dharmavit prājñaḥ satyasaṃdho 'rimardanaḥ brahmaṇyo daivataparaḥ śrīmān parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Truthful in speech, knowing dharma, wise, true to his vows, a crusher of enemies, devoted to brahmins and to the gods, glorious, a conqueror of enemy cities.

sanskrit: nalo nāma nṛpaśreṣṭho devarājasamadyutiḥ mama bhartā viśālākṣaḥ pūrṇenduvadano 'rihā
english: Nala, best of kings, resplendent as the king of gods — he is my husband, wide-eyed, with a face like the full moon, a slayer of foes.

sanskrit: āhartā kratumukhyānāṃ vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ sapatnānāṃ mṛdhe hantā ravisomasamaprabhaḥ
english: A performer of the foremost sacrifices, master of the Vedas and their auxiliaries, a slayer of rivals in battle, shining like the sun and moon together.

sanskrit: sa kaiś cin nikṛtiprajñair akalyāṇair narādhamaiḥ āhūya pṛthivīpālaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ devane kuśalair jihmair jito rājyaṃ vasūni ca
english: That king, devoted to truth and dharma, was challenged by certain wicked and base men skilled in deceit, and defeated in gambling by those crooked ones — he lost his kingdom and his wealth.

sanskrit: tasya mām avagacchadhvaṃ bhāryāṃ rājarṣabhasya vai damayantīti vikhyātāṃ bhartṛdarśanalālasām
english: Know me as the wife of that bull among kings — Damayanti, famous by name, longing to behold her husband.

sanskrit: sā vanāni girīṃś caiva sarāṃsi saritas tathā palvalāni ca ramyāṇi tathāraṇyāni sarvaśaḥ
english: I have been searching through forests and mountains, through lakes and rivers, through pleasant marshes and forests everywhere —

sanskrit: anveṣamāṇā bhartāraṃ nalaṃ raṇaviśāradam mahātmānaṃ kṛtāstraṃ ca vicarāmīha duḥkhitā
english: — seeking my husband Nala, skilled in battle, great-souled, versed in arms; I wander here in grief.

sanskrit: kaccid bhagavatāṃ puṇyaṃ tapovanam idaṃ nṛpaḥ bhavet prāpto nalo nāma niṣadhānāṃ janādhipaḥ
english: Has king Nala, lord of the Nishadas, perhaps come to this holy hermitage of your lordships?

sanskrit: yatkṛte 'ham idaṃ viprāḥ prapannā bhṛśadāruṇam vanaṃ pratibhayaṃ ghoraṃ śārdūlamṛgasevitam
english: For his sake, O brahmins, I have entered this exceedingly terrible forest — frightful, dreadful, haunted by tigers and wild beasts.

sanskrit: yadi kaiś cid ahorātrair na drakṣyāmi nalaṃ nṛpam ātmānaṃ śreyasā yokṣye dehasyāsya vimocanāt
english: If within some days and nights I do not find King Nala, I shall join myself to what is best — I shall release myself from this body.

sanskrit: ko nu me jīvitenārthas tam ṛte puruṣarṣabham kathaṃ bhaviṣyāmy adyāhaṃ bhartṛśokābhipīḍitā
english: What is the purpose of my life without that bull among men? How shall I go on, I who am afflicted today by grief for my husband?

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatīm ekām araṇye bhīmanandinīm damayantīm athocus te tāpasāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: While the daughter of Bhima, Damayanti, lamented thus alone in the forest, those truthful ascetics then spoke to her.

sanskrit: udarkas tava kalyāṇi kalyāṇo bhavitā śubhe vayaṃ paśyāma tapasā kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi naiṣadham
english: "Auspicious will be your outcome, O auspicious one, O fortunate one — we see this through our austerities. You will swiftly behold the Nishada king."

sanskrit: niṣadhānām adhipatiṃ nalaṃ ripunighātinam bhaimi dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ drakṣyase vigatajvaram
english: "You will see Nala, lord of the Nishadas, slayer of enemies, O daughter of Bhima, best among those who uphold dharma — your fever of grief will be gone."

sanskrit: vimuktaṃ sarvapāpebhyaḥ sarvaratnasamanvitam tad eva nagaraśreṣṭhaṃ praśāsantam ariṃdamam
english: "Freed from all sins, endowed with every jewel, ruling that same foremost of cities, the subduer of enemies —

sanskrit: dviṣatāṃ bhayakartāraṃ suhṛdāṃ śokanāśanam patiṃ drakṣyasi kalyāṇi kalyāṇābhijanaṃ nṛpam
english: — striking fear into his foes, dispelling grief for his friends — you shall see your husband, O auspicious one, that king of auspicious lineage."

sanskrit: evam uktvā nalasyeṣṭāṃ mahiṣīṃ pārthivātmajām antarhitās tāpasās te sāgnihotrāśramās tadā
english: Having spoken thus to the beloved queen of Nala, daughter of a king, those ascetics vanished then — along with their sacred fires and hermitage.

sanskrit: sā dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryaṃ vismitā abhavat tadā damayanty anavadyāṅgī vīrasenānṛpasnuṣā
english: Damayanti of flawless limbs, daughter-in-law of King Virasena, was filled with wonder at witnessing that great marvel.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu svapno mayā dṛṣṭaḥ ko 'yaṃ vidhir ihābhavat kva nu te tāpasāḥ sarve kva tad āśramamaṇḍalam
english: "Was this a dream I saw? What has happened here? Where have all those ascetics gone? Where is that hermitage?"

sanskrit: kva sā puṇyajalā ramyā nānādvijaniṣevitā nadī te ca nagā hṛdyāḥ phalapuṣpopaśobhitāḥ
english: "Where is that lovely river of holy waters frequented by many birds? And where are those charming trees adorned with fruits and flowers?"

sanskrit: dhyātvā ciraṃ bhīmasutā damayantī śucismitā bhartṛśokaparā dīnā vivarṇavadanābhavat
english: Having reflected long, the daughter of Bhima, Damayanti of bright smile, overcome with grief for her husband, became wretched, her face pale.

sanskrit: sā gatvāthāparāṃ bhūmiṃ bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā vilalāpāśrupūrṇākṣī dṛṣṭvāśokataruṃ tataḥ
english: Moving on to another place, her voice choked with tears, her eyes brimming with weeping, she lamented upon seeing an ashoka tree.

sanskrit: upagamya taruśreṣṭham aśokaṃ puṣpitaṃ tadā pallavāpīḍitaṃ hṛdyaṃ vihaṃgair anunāditam
english: She approached that finest of trees, the ashoka, then in bloom, bending with new shoots, lovely, resonant with birds.

sanskrit: aho batāyam agamaḥ śrīmān asmin vanāntare āpīḍair bahubhir bhāti śrīmān dramiḍarāḍ iva
english: "Ah, how this tree shines glorious in the depths of this forest, radiant with its many garlands of blossoms, like the glorious king of the Dravidians!"

sanskrit: viśokāṃ kuru māṃ kṣipram aśoka priyadarśana vītaśokabhayābādhaṃ kaccit tvaṃ dṛṣṭavān nṛpam
english: "Free me quickly from grief, O ashoka, O fair to behold — have you seen the king who is himself freed from grief, fear, and affliction?"

sanskrit: nalaṃ nāmāridamanaṃ damayantyāḥ priyaṃ patim niṣadhānām adhipatiṃ dṛṣṭavān asi me priyam
english: "Have you seen Nala, the subduer of enemies, the beloved husband of Damayanti, the lord of the Nishadas — my beloved?"

sanskrit: ekavastrārdhasaṃvītaṃ sukumāratanutvacam vyasanenārditaṃ vīram araṇyam idam āgatam
english: "Clad in half a single garment, with a body and skin delicate as a child's, that hero tormented by misfortune who has come to this forest?"

sanskrit: yathā viśokā gaccheyam aśokanaga tat kuru satyanāmā bhavāśoka mama śokavināśanāt
english: "Do that whereby I may go without grief — O ashoka tree, be true to your name, cause the destruction of my sorrow!"

sanskrit: evaṃ sāśokavṛkṣaṃ tam ārtā triḥ parigamya ha jagāma dāruṇataraṃ deśaṃ bhaimī varāṅganā
english: Having thus circumambulated that ashoka tree three times in her distress, that most excellent woman, daughter of Bhima, went on to a still more fearsome place.

sanskrit: sā dadarśa nagān naikān naikāś ca saritas tathā naikāṃś ca parvatān ramyān naikāṃś ca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
english: She saw many trees and many rivers, many lovely mountains and many beasts and birds.

sanskrit: kandarāṃś ca nitambāś ca nadāṃś cādbhutadarśanān dadarśa sā bhīmasutā patim anveṣatī tadā
english: She saw ravines and mountain slopes and streams of wondrous appearance — all this the daughter of Bhima beheld as she searched for her husband.

sanskrit: gatvā prakṛṣṭam adhvānaṃ damayantī śucismitā dadarśātha mahāsārthaṃ hastyaśvarathasaṃkulam
english: Having traveled a great distance, Damayanti of bright smile then saw a great caravan teeming with elephants, horses, and chariots.

sanskrit: uttarantaṃ nadīṃ ramyāṃ prasannasalilāṃ śubhām suśītatoyāṃ vistīrṇāṃ hradinīṃ vetasair vṛtām
english: It was crossing a lovely river with clear and auspicious waters — cool, broad, lake-like, bordered by cane reeds.

sanskrit: prodghuṣṭāṃ krauñcakuraraiś cakravākopakūjitām kūrmagrāhajhaṣākīrṇāṃ pulinadvīpaśobhitām
english: The river rang with the cries of cranes and curlews, cooed over by ruddy geese, filled with turtles, crocodiles, and fish, adorned with sandbars and islands.

sanskrit: sā dṛṣṭvaiva mahāsārthaṃ nalapatnī yaśasvinī upasarpya varārohā janamadhyaṃ viveśa ha
english: The glorious wife of Nala, that woman of shapely hips, upon seeing the great caravan, approached it and entered among the people.

sanskrit: unmattarūpā śokārtā tathā vastrārdhasaṃvṛtā kṛśā vivarṇā malinā pāṃsudhvastaśiroruhā
english: She looked like a madwoman, afflicted by grief, covered only by half a garment, gaunt, discolored, dirty, her hair matted with dust.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra manujāḥ ke cid bhītāḥ pradudruvuḥ ke cic cintāparās tasthuḥ ke cit tatra vicukruśuḥ
english: On seeing her there, some of the people fled in fear, others stood lost in thought, and some cried out.

sanskrit: prahasanti sma tāṃ ke cid abhyasūyanta cāpare cakrus tasyāṃ dayāṃ ke cit papracchuś cāpi bhārata
english: Some laughed at her, others showed disdain; some felt pity for her; and others asked her questions, O Bharata.

sanskrit: kāsi kasyāsi kalyāṇi kiṃ vā mṛgayase vane tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā vyathitāḥ smeha kaccit tvam asi mānuṣī
english: "Who are you? Whose are you, O auspicious one? What do you seek in this forest? We are troubled at the sight of you — are you perhaps a mortal woman?"

sanskrit: vada satyaṃ vanasyāsya parvatasyātha vā diśaḥ devatā tvaṃ hi kalyāṇi tvāṃ vayaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Tell us truly — are you the deity of this forest, or of this mountain, or of one of the directions? O auspicious one, we take refuge in you."

sanskrit: yakṣī vā rākṣasī vā tvam utāho 'si varāṅganā sarvathā kuru naḥ svasti rakṣasvāsmān anindite
english: "Are you a yakshini, or a rakshasi, or perhaps a most excellent woman? In any case, grant us well-being and protect us, O blameless one."

sanskrit: yathāyaṃ sarvathā sārthaḥ kṣemī śīghram ito vrajet tathā vidhatsva kalyāṇi tvāṃ vayaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Arrange things so that this entire caravan may depart from here safely and quickly, O auspicious one — we take refuge in you."

sanskrit: tathoktā tena sārthena damayantī nṛpātmajā pratyuvāca tataḥ sādhvī bhartṛvyasanaduḥkhitā sārthavāhaṃ ca sārthaṃ ca janā ye cātra ke cana
english: Thus addressed by the caravan, the virtuous Damayanti, daughter of a king, afflicted by grief over her husband's misfortune, then replied to the caravan leader, the caravan, and all who were there.

sanskrit: yūnaḥ sthavirabālāś ca sārthasya ca purogamāḥ mānuṣīṃ māṃ vijānīta manujādhipateḥ sutām nṛpasnuṣāṃ rājabhāryāṃ bhartṛdarśanalālasām
english: "Young, old, and children, and leaders of the caravan — know me as a mortal woman, daughter of a lord of men, daughter-in-law of a king, wife of a king, longing to behold my husband."

sanskrit: vidarbharāṇ mama pitā bhartā rājā ca naiṣadhaḥ nalo nāma mahābhāgas taṃ mārgāmy aparājitam
english: "My father is the king of Vidarbha; my husband is the king of Nishadha — Nala by name, greatly fortunate. I search for that unconquered one."

sanskrit: yadi jānīta nṛpatiṃ kṣipraṃ śaṃsata me priyam nalaṃ pārthivaśārdūlam amitragaṇasūdanam
english: "If you know the king, quickly tell me of my beloved — Nala, tiger among kings, slayer of troops of enemies."

sanskrit: tām uvācānavadyāṅgīṃ sārthasya mahataḥ prabhuḥ sārthavāhaḥ śucir nāma śṛṇu kalyāṇi madvacaḥ
english: The lord of the great caravan, the caravan leader named Shuchi, spoke to her of flawless limbs: "Hear my words, O auspicious one."

sanskrit: ahaṃ sārthasya netā vai sārthavāhaḥ śucismite manuṣyaṃ nalanāmānaṃ na paśyāmi yaśasvini
english: "I am the leader and guide of this caravan, O bright-smiling one. I see no man by the name of Nala, O glorious one."

sanskrit: kuñjaradvīpimahiṣaśārdūlarkṣamṛgān api paśyāmy asmin vane kaṣṭe amanuṣyaniṣevite tathā no yakṣarāḍ adya maṇibhadraḥ prasīdatu
english: "I see elephants, rhinoceroses, buffaloes, tigers, bears, and deer in this harsh forest uninhabited by humans; even so, may Manibhadra, king of yakshas, be gracious to us now."

sanskrit: sābravīd vaṇijaḥ sarvān sārthavāhaṃ ca taṃ tataḥ kva nu yāsyasi sārtho 'yam etad ākhyātum arhatha
english: She then said to all the merchants and to that caravan leader: "Where is this caravan going? Please tell me that."

sanskrit: sārthavāha uvāca sārtho 'yaṃ cedirājasya subāhoḥ satyavādinaḥ kṣipraṃ janapadaṃ gantā lābhāya manujātmaje
english: The caravan leader said: "This caravan will soon go to the realm of Subahu, the truth-speaking king of Chedi, for the purpose of profit, O daughter of a lord of men."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca sā tac chrutvānavadyāṅgī sārthavāhavacas tadā agacchat tena vai sārdhaṃ bhartṛdarśanalālasā
english: Brihadashva said: She of flawless limbs, having heard those words of the caravan leader, then set out with him, longing to behold her husband.

sanskrit: atha kāle bahutithe vane mahati dāruṇe taḍāgaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ padmasaugandhikaṃ mahat
english: Then after many days, in the great and dreadful forest, they came upon a large lake, auspicious on all sides, fragrant with lotuses.

sanskrit: dadṛśur vaṇijo ramyaṃ prabhūtayavasendhanam bahumūlaphalopetaṃ nānāpakṣigaṇair vṛtam
english: The merchants saw it was lovely, abounding in fodder and fuel, richly supplied with roots and fruits, thronged with flocks of various birds.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛṣṭasalilaṃ manoharasukhāvaham supariśrāntavāhās te niveśāya mano dadhuḥ
english: Seeing it with its clear and pleasant waters, charming and comfortable, they — their draft animals thoroughly weary — set their minds to making camp.

sanskrit: saṃmate sārthavāhasya viviśur vanam uttamam uvāsa sārthaḥ sumahān velām āsādya paścimām
english: With the caravan leader's approval, they entered that excellent forest grove; the great caravan settled in at the approach of evening.

sanskrit: athārdharātrasamaye niḥśabdastimite tadā supte sārthe pariśrānte hastiyūtham upāgamat pānīyārthaṃ girinadīṃ madaprasravaṇāvilām
english: Then at midnight, in the stillness and silence, while the caravan lay exhausted and asleep, a herd of elephants came to drink from a mountain stream turbid with the flow of their rut.

sanskrit: mārgaṃ saṃrudhya saṃsuptaṃ padminyāḥ sārtham uttamam suptaṃ mamarda sahasā ceṣṭamānaṃ mahītale
english: Blocking the path, the herd suddenly trampled the sleeping, thrashing caravan where it lay upon the ground near the lotus lake.

sanskrit: hāhāravaṃ pramuñcantaḥ sārthikāḥ śaraṇārthinaḥ vanagulmāṃś ca dhāvanto nidrāndhā mahato bhayāt ke cid dantaiḥ karaiḥ ke cit ke cit padbhyāṃ hatā narāḥ
english: The caravan folk, crying out in lamentation and seeking refuge, fled into the forest thickets, blind with sleep and overwhelmed by the great fear; some men were killed by tusks, some by trunks, some by feet.

sanskrit: gokharoṣṭrāśvabahulaṃ padātijanasaṃkulam bhayārtaṃ dhāvamānaṃ tat parasparahataṃ tadā
english: Crowded with oxen, donkeys, camels, and horses, thick with foot soldiers, that mass of people fled in terror, striking against one another.

sanskrit: ghorān nādān vimuñcanto nipetur dharaṇītale vṛkṣeṣv āsajya saṃbhagnāḥ patitā viṣameṣu ca tathā tan nihataṃ sarvaṃ samṛddhaṃ sārthamaṇḍalam
english: Uttering terrible cries they fell to the earth, dashed against trees and broken, fallen on uneven ground — so the entire prosperous company of that caravan was destroyed.

sanskrit: athāparedyuḥ saṃprāpte hataśiṣṭā janās tadā vanagulmād viniṣkramya śocanto vaiśasaṃ kṛtam bhrātaraṃ pitaraṃ putraṃ sakhāyaṃ ca janādhipa
english: When the next day came, the survivors emerged from the forest thickets, lamenting the slaughter — a brother, a father, a son, a companion, O lord of men.

sanskrit: aśocat tatra vaidarbhī kiṃ nu me duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam yo 'pi me nirjane 'raṇye saṃprāpto 'yaṃ janārṇavaḥ hato 'yaṃ hastiyūthena mandabhāgyān mamaiva tu
english: There Damayanti of Vidarbha grieved: "What evil deed have I done, that even this ocean of people that came to me in the deserted forest has been slain by the elephant herd — on account of my wretched fate?"

sanskrit: prāptavyaṃ suciraṃ duḥkhaṃ mayā nūnam asaṃśayam nāprāptakālo mriyate śrutaṃ vṛddhānuśāsanam
english: "Surely I am destined to suffer grief for a long time without doubt — one does not die before one's appointed time; this is what the teaching of the elders says."

sanskrit: yan nāham adya mṛditā hastiyūthena duḥkhitā na hy adaivakṛtaṃ kiṃ cin narāṇām iha vidyate
english: "That I today, wretched as I am, was not trampled by the elephant herd — nothing that happens to men here is not wrought by fate."

sanskrit: na ca me bālabhāve 'pi kiṃ cid vyapakṛtaṃ kṛtam karmaṇā manasā vācā yad idaṃ duḥkham āgatam
english: "Not even in childhood did I do any wrong by act, thought, or word that could have brought this suffering upon me."

sanskrit: manye svayaṃvarakṛte lokapālāḥ samāgatāḥ pratyākhyātā mayā tatra nalasyārthāya devatāḥ nūnaṃ teṣāṃ prabhāvena viyogaṃ prāptavaty aham
english: "I think the world-guardians who assembled at my svayamvara, the gods whom I rejected there for Nala's sake — surely by their power I have come to this separation."

sanskrit: evamādīni duḥkhāni sā vilapya varāṅganā hataśiṣṭaiḥ saha tadā brāhmaṇair vedapāragaiḥ agacchad rājaśārdūla duḥkhaśokaparāyaṇā
english: Having lamented thus and more, that most excellent woman, wholly given over to grief and sorrow, went on with the survivors — brahmins who had mastered the Vedas, O tiger among kings.

sanskrit: gacchantī sā cirāt kālāt puram āsādayan mahat sāyāhne cedirājasya subāhoḥ satyavādinaḥ vastrārdhakartasaṃvītā praviveśa purottamam
english: Traveling on after a long time, she reached at evening a great city — the foremost of cities of the truth-speaking king of Chedi, Subahu — and entered it, covered in half a garment.

sanskrit: tāṃ vivarṇāṃ kṛśāṃ dīnāṃ muktakeśīm amārjanām unmattām iva gacchantīṃ dadṛśuḥ puravāsinaḥ
english: The city's inhabitants saw her walking — pale, thin, wretched, her hair loose and ungroomed — looking like a madwoman.

sanskrit: praviśantīṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cedirājapurīṃ tadā anujagmus tato bālā grāmiputrāḥ kutūhalāt
english: Seeing her entering the city of the Chedi king, the village boys and children followed after her out of curiosity.

sanskrit: sā taiḥ parivṛtāgacchat samīpaṃ rājaveśmanaḥ tāṃ prāsādagatāpaśyad rājamātā janair vṛtām
english: Surrounded by them, she came near the royal palace; the queen mother, standing on the palace terrace, saw her encircled by the crowd.

sanskrit: sā janaṃ vārayitvā taṃ prāsādatalam uttamam āropya vismitā rājan damayantīm apṛcchata
english: She, O king, having turned away that crowd and brought Damayanti up to the excellent palace terrace, asked her in wonder:

sanskrit: evam apy asukhāviṣṭā bibharṣi paramaṃ vapuḥ bhāsi vidyud ivābhreṣu śaṃsa me kāsi kasya vā
english: "Even afflicted as you are by unhappiness, you bear a supreme beauty; you shine like lightning among clouds. Tell me, who are you and whose are you?"
